extracted.intended_audience: music theorists, musicology scholars, graduate students in music analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Applying Barthes's narrative-code framework to a detailed sequential musical analysis (motivic, harmonic, tonal, rhythmic, timbral) of Leos Janacek's The Fiddler's Child, mapping musical events to narrative/affective meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequential segmentation / numbered segments
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece is divided into numbered segments (forty-nine segments in the complete analysis) and each segment is analyzed (e.g., '§1 (mm. 1-3)')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segment the score by measure ranges and treat each segment as a unit for multi-dimensional analysis (tempo, motive, harmony, texture, etc.). The author uses section/segment headings (Section IA, IB, Part II, etc.) and mm. numbers to anchor interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: (MOT) Motive identification
rubrics_metrics.description: (MOT) labels motives (a, b, c, d, e, etc.), describes contour, rhythmic shape, transformations, repetition, stretto, diminution, and relationships between motives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify recurring motives, label them consistently, note variants (a1, a2, a3, b1, b2, b3), their rhythmic/melodic alterations, where they appear (which instruments/measures), and how they function narratively (e.g., motive b foretelling harm).

rubrics_metrics.name: (PIT) Pitch / pitch-class cells
rubrics_metrics.description: (PIT) records pitch collections and small pitch-class sets (e.g., 012, 024, 025, 026, 027) and specific pitch occurrences (D, Fb, Db6, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document pitch-class sets and specific pitch choices; trace how particular pitches (e.g., Fb) acquire significance by recurrence or by generating keys, whole-tone/ octatonic collections, or motivic material.

rubrics_metrics.name: (KEY) Key areas and tonality (including floating tonality)
rubrics_metrics.description: (KEY) denotes key areas and tonal behavior (e.g., E-flat Aeolian, A-flat Aeolian, floating tonality between D-flat minor and A-flat major, enharmonic spellings, Neapolitan Fb key).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map key areas across the score; note enharmonic spellings and nonfunctional/floating tonalities; consider how keys connote affect (e.g., D-flat major as a 'love key').

rubrics_metrics.name: (HAR) Harmony and harmonic function
rubrics_metrics.description: (HAR) analyzes chords, progressions, special sonorities (added seconds/sixths, ii07, w/6, quartal vs. tertian textures), and harmonic procedures (non-functional sequences, extended dominants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label chords and progressions, note recurring sonorities (e.g., c#mi w/6 connoting hopelessness), and track how harmonic choices support narrative/affective readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: (TEX) Texture and orchestration
rubrics_metrics.description: (TEX) records texture (monophonic, divisi, layered, solo vs. section), instrumental scoring (viola quartet, clarinet, harp), and textural devices (tremolo, sul ponticello, pizzicato).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe which instruments carry motives, how sectional writing (e.g., viola quartet) functions, and how texture/orchestration signal characters, groups, or narrative ambience (e.g., viola quartet as 'souls of the poor').

rubrics_metrics.name: (DYN) Dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: (DYN) documents dynamic markings (ppp, p, mf, ff, crescendo, dolcissimo) and links dynamics to affect (e.g., ppp larghetto = repose; ff interjection = disturbance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record dynamic levels and changes and interpret their contribution to mood, dramatic emphasis, and narrative turning points.

rubrics_metrics.name: (TEM) Tempo and tempo changes
rubrics_metrics.description: (TEM) records tempo markings (Vivo, Adagio, Larghetto, Con moto, Tempo I, Allegro) and tempo-related effects (accelerandi, un poco mosso) and associates them with narrative states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track tempo and tempo changes as structural markers and as expressive/narrative signals (e.g., lullaby sections marked larghetto/ppp).

rubrics_metrics.name: (RHY) Rhythm and metric layering
rubrics_metrics.description: (RHY) analyzes rhythmic motives (short 32nd groups, syncopations), metric interactions (duple layered with triple), cross-rhythms, echo effects, and metrical displacement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note repeating rhythmic cells (scasovky/entimelet), layering of meters, and how rhythmic placement creates effects such as surprise, echo, rocking (lullaby), or disturbance.

rubrics_metrics.name: I AFF I — affective reading / stated affect
rubrics_metrics.description: Author appends 'I AFF I' labels to segments to state the interpreted affect (e.g., 'I AFF I Desolation', 'I AFF I Yearning', 'I AFF I Panic').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state the affect/emotional quality being read from musical features for each segment, supporting it with motive/harmony/texture evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: {HER} Hermeneutic code / enigma notation
rubrics_metrics.description: {HER} marks hermeneutic enigmata (Enigma #1, Enigma #2) and formulates interpretive questions raised by musical events (e.g., 'Why the emphasis on Fb?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify unresolved puzzles raised by the music; enumerate enigma questions and track their development or partial resolution across segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: [PRO] Proairetic / action-oriented reading
rubrics_metrics.description: [PRO] links musical events to narrative actions or causal sequences (e.g., 'The fiddler is coming out of his reminiscence', 'Someone has died').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proairetic readings to map musical progressions to implied or stated narrative events; document when music signals actions or plot developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: [JAN] Composer's writings and direct testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: [JAN] cites Janacek's essay/letters and composer statements (e.g., 'The Fiddler pining', 'falling asleep' motive) as evidence for interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate composer-authored commentary and contemporaneous writings as primary evidence for motive meaning and rhetorical function.

rubrics_metrics.name: {REF} Referential / intertextual evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: {REF} brings in external musical references (folk music resemblance, other Janacek works, Wagner, Dvorak, whole-tone/octatonic allusions) to support meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare motifs/sonorities to folk tunes, other works, or cultural practices to build intertextual arguments (e.g., linking a motive to Moravian folk modes or to offstage chorus traditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: [POEM] Source-text concordance
rubrics_metrics.description: [POEM] aligns musical segments with lines from the poem on which the piece is based, using poem text to corroborate narrative interpretations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference musical passages with the poem's stanzas/lines to justify programmatic readings (e.g., 'An old fiddler died' aligning with funeral-march musical material).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivic-character mapping (instrumental/persona assignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign motives and/or instrumental groups to characters or social forces (e.g., 'viola quartet' = 'souls of the poor'; motive d = 'the mayor / law').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recurrence, timbre, register, and textual cues to map musical materials to characters/groups; track how mappings evolve (omnipresence, transference, extension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of motivic transference and anti-transference law
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes Janacek's 'strange law' prohibiting motivic exchange between instruments and allowed exceptions (transference between closely related instruments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect or note the composer's stated norms about motivic assignment when interpreting motive transference; treat exceptions as interpretively significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set-class / scale-type analysis (whole-tone, octatonic, quartal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify scale/collection types (whole-tone, octatonic-0/1/2, octatonic segments, quartal harmony) and their narrative/mystical associations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label which non-diatonic collections are operative in segments and consider historical/associative meanings (e.g., octatonic associated with mysticism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Associative meaning of specific sonorities/keys
rubrics_metrics.description: Associate recurring sonorities or keys with stable semantic meanings (e.g., 'c#mi w/6' = hopelessness; 'D-flat major' = profound goodness/love; 'barn owl' ritornello = harbinger of death).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish semantic value for particular sonorities by demonstrating consistent usage across works or across multiple presentations within the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of orchestral/sonic tropes as cultural signifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret instruments/sonorities as culturally coded signs (e.g., harp = heaven/angels; offstage chorus = nature/regeneration or in this case sorrow/inequity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use timbral stereotypes and performance practice to support narrative inferences; weigh counter-evidence when the trope differs (e.g., Beckerman's thesis vs. this analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal devices: ritornello, recurrence, and their semantic functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify formal devices (ritornello indicated in reduction) and their recurrent semantic roles (ritornello representing 'souls of the poor' or recurring harmonic/ motivic functions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map recurring formal returns (ritornello, ostinato) to stable narrative or affective referents and document changes across recurrences that shift meaning (e.g., increasing despair).
